continuous_timed_transcript.text: The economy is showing impressive resilience.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: Even with recent shocks, the trends are positive and reveal solid growth.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: Job gains have kept pace with the workforce,
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: and the unemployment rate has changed little.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: Yeah, so let me go back to first principles, Nick.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: I don't believe that either part of our mandate is generally at war with the other part.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: I do not believe that price stability and full employment is an either-or proposition.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: There have been policymakers over the last several generations who have thought that there is a strict tradeoff there.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: Any central banker, especially a central banker where the labor markets are more or less at equilibrium—
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: any central banker, when he or she sees underlying inflation moving higher—
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh

continuous_timed_transcript.text: he or she is more inclined to tighten policy.
continuous_timed_transcript.speaker: Kevin Warsh
